text.p: Italian bonds and futures maintained their buoyant tone, fuelled by dollar strength and a subsequent firming of the lira, but the 10-year Btp closed off its day's high and volume was thin, dealers said.
"Btps haven't seen good volume or big interest today," said one trader. The LIFFE Dec contract closed up 18 basis points at 123.16, but off its day's high of 123.60.
"Btps have remained quite high on the back of the dollar," the trader added. "There's still a very good spread." The Btp-bund spread narrowed to 223 bps from an earlier 232.

Dealers said they saw no clouds on the horizon and said optimism over EMU was still underpinning the market, especially given Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi's comments on Monday night reiterating Italy's determination to take the lira back into the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) by year-end.
"This market's got no intention of going down," said another dealer.
"As soon as certain levels are reached, the money comes back in."
